title: Intrauterine Stent Placement Following Hysteroscopic Septum Resection
official: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Intrauterine Stent Placement Following Hysteroscopic Septum Resection
summary: The study hopes to learn the best way to prevent internal scar tissue after septum removal. The use of an intrauterine foley catheter balloon may prevent the formation of adhesions following surgery.

interventions.name: Intraoperative placement of an inflated intrauterine pediatric foley catheter

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 and above
* Patients electing to undergo hysteroscopic septoplasty following an informed consent and shared decision making process
* Uterine septum of at least 50% of the uterine cavity length as quantified on 3-dimensional saline infusion ultrasound

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unwilling or unable to provide informed consent
* History of prior uterine septum resection
* History of prior transmural uterine surgery
* Preexisting intrauterine adhesions or prior treatment for intrauterine adhesions
* Individuals in whom complete septum resection is unable to be performed as a single procedure
sponsor: Weill Medical College of Cornell University
